Merged, thanks for sharing. Looks good.

The main idea behind MOOCs on FutureLearn is to alternate between different teaching methods: videos, articles and coding tutorials. In other words no focus on "video only". In total, the required workload per week is 4 hours, after which students have a good understanding of Gaussian process modelling, statistical  shape modelling, model-based image analysis AND can program their own model-based medical image analysis application. So the course **does** cover the topic in a comprehensive manner ... just not in video only. Then again this list is called cs-"video"-courses :/
Direct videos for this are not readily available for viewing/download.

Thank you for the pull request. I am afraid I would not like to merge this pull request. Why?

University level courses are often rigorous and hard to find, but there are tens of thousands of tutorials on youtube, anyone can make tutorials but everyone cannot make University grade video courses.

That is why  I created separate page for Java, Physics/Math and engineering courses, so that this page should do one thing and do it well. Please feel free to manage a SDET resource page, you may share the link in this PR so that others can benefit from your effort.

Thank you,
